run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-26T03:03:50Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is explained by the checkout service being completely unavailable, not by a fault inside frontend. The firing rule (group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal) evaluates sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0 with duration 180s; both frontend (3.133) and frontend-proxy (1.511) are firing with activeAt 2026-11-26T03:03:50Z. Frontend error spans are concentrated on POST /api/checkout and its oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span, whose exact error is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.235.183:8080', and 10.96.235.183 is the ClusterIP of the checkout Service. The checkout Service has only a notReadyAddress and no ready endpoints, because the checkout Deployment (generation 4, 0 ready / 1 unavailable replicas) was updated at 2026-11-26T03:03:01Z by the field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98..., whose digest the registry reports as 'not found'; the replacement pod is Pending in ImagePullBackOff and the previous healthy pod (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout) was deleted at 03:03:03Z. Frontend error spans therefore rise from ~03:03 onward (error-span counter 59 -> 133 -> 251 -> 376 -> 533 between 03:01:30 and 03:06:45). Frontend itself is ready with 0 restarts and its non-checkout routes still returned 200. All flagd fault-injection flags were off, and no other otel-demo Deployment was modified, so those candidates were rejected.

claims.text: The HighRequestErrorRate rule for the frontend goldensignal group evaluates sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0 with duration 180s, and at 03:06:50 its firing instances are service_name=frontend (value 3.1333, activeAt 2026-11-26T03:03:50Z) and service_name=frontend-proxy (value 1.5111, same activeAt).

Frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0 at 02:59, 03:00 and 03:01, then 0.0444/s at 03:02, 0.0444/s at 03:03, 0.8222/s at 03:04, 2.70/s at 03:05, 2.70/s at 03:06 and 3.1333/s at 03:07; the underlying counter for frontend error spans was 0 until 02:56:45, 55 at 02:57:00 (flat until 03:01:15), 59 at 03:01:30, then 133 at 03:03:45, 251 at 03:04:45, 376 at 03:05:45 and 533 at 03:06:45.

Frontend error spans are concentrated on the checkout path: span_name POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect, while GET /api/data and oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rates stay ~0.01-0.03/s.

The exact failure recorded on the frontend oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.235.183:8080', with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_code=ERROR; the enclosing frontend POST /api/checkout and executing api route spans returned http.status_code 500, and the same trace shows frontend-proxy POST 'router frontend egress' 500 and a load-generator POST span 500.

The frontend container log carries the same error: level 50 err.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.235.183:8080' from the placeOrder client call, followed by 'POST /api/checkout' with http.response.status_code 500, repeatedly between 03:06:19 and 03:06:29.
10.96.235.183, the address that refused the frontend's connection, is the ClusterIP of the Service checkout (port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout).
The checkout Endpoints object has no ready addresses at all: its only entry is subsets[0].notReadyAddresses = 10.244.2.242 (pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-g9tmp).

Deployment otel-demo/checkout has status.replicas=1, status.unavailableReplicas=1 and no readyReplicas/availableReplicas (0 of 1 available) at generation 4, while every other otel-demo Deployment reports 1 ready and 1 available.

Pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-g9tmp (created 2026-11-26T03:03:08Z, owner ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4) is Pending with Ready=False/ContainersNotReady; its checkout container has restartCount 0 and state.waiting.reason=ImagePullBackOff with message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a": ErrImagePull ... not found'.

ReplicaSet checkout-64c65899fc (deployment revision 1, created 02:55:32Z) ran image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout and now has 0 replicas, while ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4 (revision 2, created 03:03:01Z) has 1 replica and specifies image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a; the frontend and frontend-proxy pods still run ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-frontend and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-frontend-proxy.

otel-demo events show the rollout sequence for checkout: Deployment checkout 'Scaled up replica set checkout-7ffc7768f4 from 0 to 1' at 03:03:01Z and 03:03:08Z, ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4 SuccessfulCreate 03:03:01Z/03:03:08Z, the old pod checkout-64c65899fc-l4xdz 'Stopping container checkout' (Killing) and 'Deleted pod' at 03:03:03Z, and repeated Pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-*/g9tmp Warning Failed 'Failed to pull image ... not found' / 'Error: ErrImagePull' from 03:03:04Z to 03:06:17Z.

Deployment otel-demo/checkout was last written by field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' (operation Update) at 2026-11-26T03:03:01Z, after the initial helm Apply at 02:55:29Z, and its current pod-template image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98...; it is the only otel-demo Deployment with generation > 1 and the only one with a writer other than helm or kube-controller-manager (all 25 others are generation 1, helm-applied, with github/open-telemetry, postgres or valkey images).

Other otel-demo services' own error rates stayed at or near zero over 02:40-03:07: accounting 0 throughout, agent 0 from 03:01 onward, checkout 0.0037/s (a single error span pair POST / oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder at 03:06), whereas frontend was 3.13/s, frontend-proxy 1.51/s and load-generator 0.80/s at 03:07.

The frontend pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-5p7br is Running with restartCount 0 and ready, and a trace sample at 03:01 shows frontend GET /api/data and oteldemo.AdService/GetAds returning 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code=0, so the frontend's own process was serving non-checkout traffic while it failed the checkout path.

The HighRequestErrorRate alert for frontend is caused by the checkout Deployment being rolled to an image reference the registry cannot resolve at 03:03:01Z, which removed the only ready checkout backend, made the checkout Service ClusterIP (10.96.235.183:8080) refuse connections, and turned the frontend's POST /api/checkout into gRPC 14 / HTTP 500 errors; frontend-proxy and load-generator show their own 500 error spans on the same request path.

A flagd feature-flag fault (for example a checkout/payment/cart failure variant) is not the cause: every flag in the otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap is state=ENABLED with defaultVariant=off, and no checkout-specific fault flag is present.

A fault inside frontend itself is not supported: the frontend pod is ready with 0 restarts, its non-checkout routes returned 200 in traces, and every frontend error log/trace names the checkout Service IP with ECONNREFUSED rather than a frontend-internal error.

Not all frontend error spans originate in the incident: a first batch of 55 frontend error spans appears at 02:57:00 (after the 02:55 namespace deploy, when the old checkout pod checkout-64c65899fc-l4xdz was serving and ready), the counter then stays flat at 55 until 03:01:15, and the 1m error rate is 0 at every sample from 02:58:30 to 03:01:30 - so that early batch precedes the checkout image change and is background, not the cause of the sustained rise after 03:03.

Restore checkout capacity by reverting the checkout Deployment's pod-template image to the previously working ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout (revision 1 / ReplicaSet checkout-64c65899fc), then confirm the checkout Endpoints repopulate with ready addresses and the frontend POST /api/checkout 500s stop; separately review the 03:03:01Z change applied by the 'OpenAPI-Generator' field manager, since that is the write that introduced the unresolvable digest.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what process or person wrote Deployment checkout as field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-26T03:03:01Z, and why the unresolvable digest quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64@sha256:20c6ce98... was chosen, could not be verified.

Logs of the previous checkout pod checkout-64c65899fc-l4xdz are unobtainable because the pod was deleted at 03:03:03Z, so checkout-side behaviour immediately before the rollout could not be inspected.

Error/latency status of the other otel-demo services (payment, email, shipping, cart, currency, product-catalog, fraud-detection, kafka, ad, recommendation) was not established: with the exception of accounting, agent and checkout, no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series came back for them in the queries run, which is unknown rather than zero.

Traces are a biased sample of spans with omitted spans unknown, so the complete call graph and a precise failed-request count are not established; the growth of the error rate from ~03:03 to 03:07 (rather than a flat plateau at the load rate) was not explained by the evidence collected.

Whether the alert on frontend-proxy (1.511) has any contributor other than pass-through 500s on POST /api/checkout was not fully separated, although its error spans in the inspected trace are the same checkout request.
next_steps: Have an operator roll the checkout Deployment back to the known-good image and verify that checkout Endpoints gain a ready address and frontend 5xx on /api/checkout stops.
Audit the 03:03:01Z write on Deployment otel-demo/checkout attributed to field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' in cluster audit logs (outside these tools) to identify the actor and prevent recurrence.
Add alerting or admission checks for unresolvable image references/digests so a rollout to a non-existent image is caught before it drains the sole replica of a dependency.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name=="flagd-config") | (.data["demo.flagd.json"] | fromjson).flags | to_entries | map({flag: .key, state: .value.state, defaultVariant: .value.defaultVariant})

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows Prometheus's state at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window; it cannot show the state when the incident happened.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
